title: Models and Gene Therapies for AAT Deficiency-Core A
text: Core A Project Summary The Vector Immunology Core (Core A) will directly support all Projects of this program project grant by providing reliable, consistent and standardized immunological assays. Core A will create, validate and perform immunological assays to characterize B-cell and T-cell immune responses to adeno-associated virus (AAV) and lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vehicles, transgene products, and editing enzymes in mice and ferrets. Core A will: evaluate innate immune responses to gene therapies by evaluating complement activation and cytokine levels; characterize B-cell responses by transduction inhibition-based neutralizing antibody assays and anti- transgene antibodies; characterize T-cell responses by enzyme-linked immunoSPOT (ELISPOT) assays; and evaluate cytokine production through both enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) and flow cytometry- based cytokine bead assays. The core will also produce novel immune modulatory therapeutics and AAV- specific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-regulatory cells (Tregs). Overall, Core A will generate valuable data while providing all necessary support and resources to the Projects in this program project grant. This will further our understanding of the role of the immune system in gene editing and gene therapies.

title: Bacteriophage virus-like particle vaccines for Chlamydia trachomatis urogenital infection
text:
Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common bacterial sexually transmitted infection, causing infertility, ectopic
pregnancy, and pelvic inflammatory disease in women. Despite the availability of effective treatment, the
prevalence of chlamydia continues to rise, highlighting the need for a prophylactic vaccine. This proposal
seeks to identify Chlamydia trachomatis vaccine candidates by investigating the functions of antibodies to
specific epitopes of Chlamydia trachomatis proteins involved in binding and entering host cells, providing a
novel approach for Chlamydia trachomatis vaccine development.

title: A Novel Combinatorial Approach Targeting Neurodegeneration in Familial Dysautonomia
text:
Familial dysautonomia (FD) is a neurodegenerative inherited disease caused by a splicing mutation in the ELP1
gene that results in variable skipping of exon 20. This work aims to develop a novel gene-editing strategy for
ELP1 and generate critical in vivo proof-of-concept data to assess the efficacy and potential synergy of a
combinatorial therapy for the devastating neurodegeneration characteristic of FD. This approach combines a
small molecule splicing modulator compound (SMC) with a gene editing approach.

title: Epigenetic regulation of exhausted CD8 T cells via the miR-29a-TET2 axis
text:
Chronic infections and cancer result in dysfunction of immune cells, termed “exhaustion”. With
this proposal, we will investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms that cause exhaustion
and the use of a small non-coding RNA (microRNA-29a; miR-29a) to overcome exhaustion. We
will explore the potential of delivering miR-29a to T cells as a novel strategy to improve
responses to immunotherapy.

title: Investigating the Impact of Adolescent Social Experiences on Neurodevelopmental Regulators of Addiction Susceptibility
text:
Social experiences during adolescence are critical for the formation and stabilization of decision-making circuits
that regulate drug use susceptibility. Here, we will combine innovative behavioral and computational methods
with circuit-specific single-cell genomics assays to interrogate the neurodevelopmental mechanisms that are
altered by adolescent social isolation and associated with greater risk for addiction-like behaviors.

title: Integrating Epidemiologic and Genomic Data to Elucidate the Genetic Overlap Between Congenital Anomalies and Pediatric Cancer
text:
In our prior work, we have identified multiple novel congenital anomaly-cancer associations by linking data
from population-based birth-defects and cancer registries from four states. Here, we propose to expand this
study to seven additional states to analyze a cohort representing >25 million live births and approximately 35%
of the US population. We will also search for genetic mechanisms driving these associations through the
analysis of whole-genome sequencing data in 20,000 children with congenital anomalies or pediatric cancer,
including 2000 sequenced tumors.

title: Elucidating the complex allosteric regulation of PFK-1, a broadly evolutionarily conserved glycolytic enzyme
text:
Allosteric regulation of enzymes, which underpins many metabolic processes, can be perturbed by genetic
mutations, contributing to metabolic re-programming in cancer and other diseases. The broadly evolutionarily
conserved enzyme phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) is allosterically regulated by many small molecules to control
glycolytic flux in the cell, but the evolution and molecular mechanism of this regulation is poorly understood. We
propose to characterize the complex combinatorial allosteric mechanism of PFK-1 towards the rational design
of powerful therapeutics to target this essential enzyme in metabolic diseases and cancer.

title: Spatial Organization in Biochemical Reaction Networks
text:
Biological networks are often spatially organized to ensure that reactions inside cells occur at the
right place and time, particularly in fundamental processes like cell signaling and genome
regulation. We will systematically explore the relationship between spatial organization and
function in these systems with quantitative biochemical assays, structural methods, cell-based
studies, and new synthetic biology tools. This approach will enable us to understand underlying
regulatory principles and how to intervene when these processes are misregulated in human
diseases.

title: Bioinformatics Analysis of Next Generation Sequencing Data from Cancer Cells
text:
Sequence-based assays provide a powerful toolset for gaining insight into the function and disfunction of
cancer cells. Unfortunately, the resulting data sets are a classic example of “big data” and experimental
biologists are traditionally not trained to handle or analyze them. The goal of this R50 proposal is to
provide Dr. Bartom’s expertise in both computation and biology to the cancer research programs of the
Robert H. Lurie Comprehensive Cancer Center, and more specifically to the Quantitative Data Sciences
Core (QDSC).

title: Multimodal classification and sub-cellular compartmentalization of displaced amacrine cells in the mouse retina
text:
Amacrine cells are the final remaining neuron class in the retina in which there are substantial gaps in our
knowledge of cell types, and this project will fill part of this gap in knowledge by establishing a multimodal
classification of displaced amacrine cells. Amacrine cells are also among the most important examples of
subcellular compartmentalization in neuroscience, so a second goal our project is to reveal how they
compartmentalize function in different parts of their neuritic arbors. Revealing the identities of amacrine cell types
and their roles in retinal computation will help us understand their dysfunction in disease.

title: Non-invasive fetal HLA and KIR genotyping of cell-free DNA from maternal blood
text:
Developing non-invasive approaches to assess preeclampsia risk in early stages of gestation is
urgently needed. We will leverage our expertise in analyzing immune system genes that affect
preeclampsia risk to develop a genotyping assay that targets fetal cell-free DNA circulating in maternal
blood. This approach can pave the way for developing a new prognostic biomarker for fetal-maternal
health in early stages.

title: Project 1 - HEARTSPOT: Evaluating a Machine Learning System to Aid Decision-Making in the Emergency Department for Patients with ADRD
text:
OTHER PROJECT INFORMATION – Project Narrative
An emergency department clinician treating a patient with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) faces difficult
decisions about whether to recommend invasive treatment. If the patient is cognitively impaired, assessing health
risks and benefits is even more complex. This project will test a machine learning tool called HEARTSPOT that
presents a report to help clinicians make this difficult decision. HEARTSPOT will examine each patient’s medical
history faster and more completely than any human could and present a summary of its findings to the emergency
department clinician in real time.

title: Eliciting Broadly Neutralizing Antibody Responses against HIV-1 Fusion Peptide Epitope by AB Toxin B Subunit-Based Immunogens
text:
Innovative ideas are crucial for developing an effective HIV/AIDS vaccine. The aim of this project is to create
AB toxin-based vaccines with the capability to elicit broadly neutralizing antibodies targeting the fusion peptide
region of HIV-1 and capable of neutralizing Tier 2 viruses, ultimately paving the way for a protective vaccine.

title: Graduate Training Program in Computational Biology, Bioinformatics and Biomedical Data Science (CBB)
text: The rapid advances in high-throughput biology and digital biomedicine as well as machine learning and data science technologies have created critical needs and an unprecedented opportunity to train the next generation of multidisciplinary researchers at the interface of biomedical and computational sciences. This new T32 predoctoral training program aims to enhance graduate research training in the areas of computational biology, bioinformatics, and biomedical data science. It will be a cross-campus program with a collaborative team science environment and evidence-based, reproducible, and responsible research conduct to ensure scientific rigor for transformative workforce development.

title: HNF4A as a mediator of environmental risk in IBD
text:
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a complex disease with genetic and environmental risk factors combining
to cause lifelong intestinal disease with treatment regimens that are often inadequate. We find that the balance
of hepatocyte nuclear receptor 4 alpha (HNF4α) isoforms is disrupted in IBD patients, which is further
exacerbated by exposure to environmental IBD risk factors. We propose to determine how HNF4α isoform
imbalance drives the onset and progression of IBD by integrating signals from environmental risk factors to gain
new insights into IBD pathophysiology and identify new avenues for therapy.

title: Mechanisms of Parp inhibitor-induced bone marrow toxicities
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it focuses on understanding how a class of drugs
called PARP inhibitors, drugs being used to treat cancer and being tested for an expanding number of non-
malignant human diseases, cause the serious blood and bone marrow toxicities seen in some patients taking
them. This proposal will provide key mechanistic insight into which cells in the bone marrow require the
enzymes targeted by these drugs for normal functioning, and whether these drugs have the capability to
mutate the DNA of these cells to predispose patients to bone marrow failure or blood cancers. Thus, the
proposed research is relevant to the National Heart, Blood, and Lung Institute’s mission to promote the
prevention of blood diseases and enhance the health of all individuals so that they can live longer and more
fulfilling lives.

title: CELLENONE X1 NEO SYSTEM FOR PROTEOMICS RESEARCH
text:
Baylor College of Medicine is committed to advancing cutting-edge biomedical research through the integration
of state-of-the-art technologies. To establish new capabilities in single-cell and spatial proteomic profiling at our
institution, we are seeking funding for the cellenONE X1 Neo system. This innovative platform will empower
our investigators to explore disease processes and developmental mechanisms with unprecedented resolution,
significantly accelerating insights into a wide range of conditions impacting human health.

title: Statistical methods for population-level cell-type-specific analyses of tissue omics data for Alzheimer's disease
text:
Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the major cause of dementia and selectively affects certain brain cell types. However,
current single-cell technology limits the ability to study this on a large scale across multiple omics, such as DNA,
RNA, and protein. To fill this knowledge gap, we will develop and implement statistical methods that will leverage
existing rich tissue-level and limited single-cell omics data, with the goals of increasing our understanding of
cellular mechanisms underlying AD and informing future prevention and treatment strategies.

title: Research Framework for Innovation in Read Mapping
text:
Mapping sequenced DNA or RNA reads to a reference human genome or pan-genome is the first essential
step in variant calling, reference-based assembly, gene expression quantification, and nearly all other genomics
analyses. However, read mapping, despite over two decades of progress, remains one of the most computationally
expensive steps in any pipeline and faster, more memory efficient, and more flexible algorithms are needed to
reduce cost and increase mapping accuracy. To achieve this, we propose a “meta” approach that will develop
a software platform for innovation and rapid experimentation with new ideas in read mapping that will improve
mapping software.

title: Creation of a knowledgebase of high quality assertions of the clinical actionability of somatic variants in cancer
text:
Cancer is driven by DNA mutations which can increasingly be used to determine the type, likely outcome and
best treatment options for individual patients. Establishing the clinical relevance of each mutation requires
experts to review and summarize a growing body of evidence. By coordinating the efforts of these disease
experts we will build a database of mutations and information that helps doctors guide treatment of cancer
patients.
